evals.name: slack-notifier-bypass
evals.expected_output: Surfaces that the existing NotificationChannel registry (notifications/base.py) wraps every channel's send() through a shared RateLimiter, and that the proposed standalone SlackNotifier/send_slack_message plan would bypass both the registry and the rate limiter. Recommends implementing Slack as a registered NotificationChannel subclass instead.
expectations: Names the existing NotificationChannel registry/base class as the mechanism to extend, not a new standalone class
Explicitly flags that the proposed plan bypasses the shared RateLimiter guard in NotificationChannel.send()
Frames this as material guidance (would change the implementation approach), not routine orientation

evals.name: dropbox-image-fetch
evals.expected_output: Surfaces core/net.py's is_allowed_remote_host() SSRF guard and get_session() convention, already used by the one existing remote-fetch integration (webhook_fetcher.py), and flags that the proposed raw requests.get(url) plan skips both -- a security-relevant omission.
expectations: Names is_allowed_remote_host() (or the SSRF/internal-host guard it implements) as something the new fetch path must use
Names the shared get_session()/webhook_fetcher.py convention as precedent to follow instead of a bare requests.get() call
Frames this as a security-relevant material finding, with high or medium confidence, not a passing mention

evals.name: device-sensor-unique-id
evals.expected_output: Surfaces that sensor.kind exists specifically to distinguish multiple sensors on the same device (entities/sensor.py), so dropping the ':{kind}' suffix from unique_id() would collide a device's temperature/humidity/battery sensors onto one ID. Flags the proposed migration as unsafe as stated and recommends a real discriminator stay in the ID (or an explicit collision-handling plan).
expectations: Explicitly names the collision risk: multiple sensors on one device would get the same ID if the ':{kind}' suffix is dropped
Connects entities/sensor.py's per-subclass kind attribute to why registry.py's unique_id() includes it
Recommends against the simplification as proposed, or names the collision as something that must be resolved before proceeding, rather than endorsing the task's framing that the suffix is unnecessary

evals.name: retry-helper-unification
evals.expected_output: Surfaces that with_retry (core/retry.py) fails open (swallows the exception, returns None) while call_with_retry (integrations/retry_utils.py) fails closed (re-raises), and that this is a real behavioral difference each call site depends on -- nightly_sync.py relies on the None-means-skip contract, charge.py relies on the exception propagating. Flags this as a genuine decision the unification must resolve, not a mechanical merge.
expectations: Names the fail-open vs fail-closed behavioral difference between the two helpers explicitly
Connects this to a concrete consequence for at least one call site (nightly_sync.py's result-is-None branch, or charge.py needing the exception to propagate)
Treats this as an open decision / genuine ambiguity to resolve before merging, rather than silently picking one behavior or treating the merge as purely mechanical deduplication
